summary: Divergence audit of the Phase 4.2 boxI_lift blocker. VERDICT: the direct route is COMPLETABLE; the [BLOCKED] should be LIFTED, not routed to a follow-up. The 3-cycle counterexample in handoffs/04 refutes only boxI_lift stated over an ARBITRARY finite Graph. It does NOT refute the tree-restricted boxI_lift soundness actually needs, because no NIK constructor can build a cyclic raw graph: only boxI (Deduction.lean:297) and diaE (:309) add edges, each addEdge x y with y a cofinitely-fresh sink and x pre-existing, starting from Graph.trivial (:316). So the raw R-graph of every derivation is a finite rooted forest by construction. This is exactly the invariant Simpson's published soundness proof relies on (Simpson1994 Lemma 8.1.3 is stated 'Let G be a tree'; his 8.1.2 boxI case reads 'Let G'=G u {xRy} which is a tree as y is not in G' -- chunks 0154-0156, read directly). CSLib's landed cs5FCIncest_lift (F1) / cs5FCIncest_raise (F2) are the exact analogues of the F1/F2 Simpson's Lifting-Lemma cascade uses. The earlier INTRACTABLE/GATE-C verdicts predate and are superseded by the Phase 1-3 box_iff_base/dia_iff_base breakthrough that dissolved the consumer-side exact-symmetry wall; the ONLY residual is the boxI producer lift = the tree cascade. Recommended: fold IsDerivationForest (X.Finite + graded rank + unique-parent) into the Phase 5 motive (discharged at Graph.trivial, preserved per constructor), and complete boxI_lift as a standalone lemma taking that invariant + raw edge-cond as hypotheses, reusing boxI_raise_step per node.
